GUS Technology Launches XNO® Battery Products — Echion Technologies
GUS Technology Launches XNO® Battery Products

Tokyo, Japan — GUS Technology today announced the launch of a new range of fast-charging, high power battery products produced at its manufacturing facilities in Zhongli, Taiwan. The launch, announced at Battery Japan, builds on GUS’ product portfolio which targets high-power industrial and infrastructure applications.

Compared with lithium titanate (LTO), a chemistry commonly used in high-power battery applications, XNO® offers more than 50% higher energy density while maintaining fast-charging capability, long cycle life, and safety characteristics. This combination enables longer operating runtimes without compromising the durability and operational safety expected from high-power battery systems.

GUS Technology’s XNO® products have already begun customer trials in on-highway applications, with further opportunities in other sectors. GUS Technology’s new XNO® products are now available for general customer sampling, and detailed specifications will be unveiled at Battery Japan.

“XNO® technology was developed to deliver fast-charging and high-power performance without the energy density and lifetime limitations seen in traditional high-power lithium-ion chemistries,” said Dr Jean de La Verpilliere, CEO at Echion Technologies. “We have been impressed with GUS’ capabilities and are excited to see XNO® incorporated into their product offering.”

GUS Technology’s established battery manufacturing infrastructure at Zhongli, Taiwan has an annual production capacity of approximately 1 GWh and supplies battery systems to customers across North America, Europe, and Asia for applications including industrial equipment, transportation systems, and data centre power infrastructure.

The case for recycling lithium-ion batteries at their end of life is compelling: it reduces waste, lowers the carbon footprint of battery manufacture, and retains material value. A nascent battery recycling industry is therefore emerging, deploying pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical techniques to retrieve critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel from today’s Li-ion batteries.

Echion is seeking to recover anode material not only from batteries that reach their end of life, but also from production scrap – such as offcuts from coated electrode rolls – which inevitably arise during manufacturing. Typically, around 5-10% of material is lost as scrap during cell production.
Conventional pyrometallurgical or hydrometallurgical recycling processes rely on high temperatures or strong acids to recover valuable elements such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, copper and manganese.
Ramon Cabiscol, Senior Process Engineer at Echion explains:

XNO® is very hard to dissolve in acid, which makes it difficult to process using conventional methods. However, this offers a good opportunity for ‘direct’ recycling – using milder processes to recover the anode material, typically by delaminating or stripping apart the binder and separating it from the metal current-collectors.”
